# kemp_header_rule (Resource)

Manages a header rule that adds, deletes or replaces an HTTP header. Attach it to a virtual service's request_rules or response_rules.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kemp_header_rule" "env" {
  name   = "add_env_header"
  action = "add"
  header = "X-Environment"
  value  = "production"
}

resource "kemp_header_rule" "host" {
  name    = "rewrite_host"
  action  = "replace"
  header  = "Host"
  pattern = "internal\\.example\\.com"
  value   = "www.example.com"
}

resource "kemp_header_rule" "server" {
  name   = "strip_server_header"
  action = "delete"
  header = "Server"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) add, delete or replace. Can be changed in place.
- `header` (String) Header to add or modify. For delete, a pattern matching the header names to remove.
- `name` (String) Rule name: letters, digits and underscores. Changing this forces a new rule.

### Optional

- `pattern` (String) For replace: the text in the header's value to replace. Required for replace, not used otherwise.
- `value` (String) For add: the header value. For replace: the replacement text. Required for both, not used for delete.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The rule name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Rules are imported by name.
terraform import kemp_header_rule.example my_rule_name
```
